correctness.rationale: For every m>=2 and c_i,d,B>0 the centered vector x with hubs +/-sqrt(d)/2 and reflected leaves +/-[sqrt(c_i)+sqrt(d)/2] has norm square K and squared edge differences exactly the purchasing prices. Hence Rayleigh gives lambda2<=B/K for ANY independently weighted feasible competitor, asymmetric or with zero conductances. The proposed weights spend B, are positive, and satisfy Lx=(B/K)x. In the reflection-even orthogonal-to-constants space the nonzero Rayleigh quotients are at least min(w_i)>B/K. In the odd sector the positive eigenvector v yields the exact ground-state sum-of-squares yT(M-lambda I)y=sum_i w_i*v_h*v_i*(y_i/v_i-y_h/v_h)^2; every coefficient is positive, so lambda=B/K is the simple lowest odd eigenvalue. Therefore it is the simple Fiedler eigenvalue. Equality in the fixed-vector Rayleigh bound forces each pendant rate independently by its leaf equation and the bridge by a hub equation, proving global uniqueness. The m=2 example gives K=83/2 and lambda=200/83. Independent separately written Fraction/numpy checker verified 252 exact rational budget, eigenvector, energy and spectral instances for m=2..8; finite checks are not the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the heterogeneous reflected price-vector closed form and unique independent-edge allocation, not for the general fastest-mixing SDP dual, uniform-cost double brooms, homogeneous two-side-price double stars, or general tree-embedding method. Primary Sun/Boyd/Xiao/Diaconis establishes arbitrary linear costs as a general SDP and dual embedding, without this evaluated vector-price family. Richter/Rocha computes unit-priced double-broom absolute connectivity. Göring/Helmberg/Wappler establish general optimal embedding/separator/dimension theory, not the explicit all-pair-price optimization. The most relevant fully inspected published mathematical finding has two constant pendant price classes, not unequal prices across mirrored pairs. No implication from those special classes produces a formula for all c_i. Fiedler 1990 full text was not accessible (only the published uniform-price abstract, and authorized retrieval blocked by disconnected VPN); this is a stated risk, not an automatic originality failure.

value.rationale: The object is a natural fixed-topology network design problem (algebraic connectivity of a two-hub tree) with actual heterogeneity: m independent positive paired acquisition prices, an independent bridge price, independent rates on 2m+1 edges, and no imposed symmetry on competitors. The exact B/K and all-edge unique allocation give a directly usable optimal design and a structural inverse-square-root law that cannot be read off from the known homogeneous-price double-star theorem. Showing uniqueness among asymmetric competitors and simple Fiedler eigenvalue adds substantive rigidity. The result is a complete natural classification for reflected pair prices, not an arbitrary finite slice or generic SDP restatement; no general unrelated downstream theorem is required.
